column4: Initial introduction of the SysAdmin team to Kubernetes deployments. Manual creation of pipelines for each application environment (Dev, UAT, and Prod). Frequent syntax errors resulted in pipeline execution failures.

Invalid memory request limits resulted in Out-Of-Memory (OOM) Killed statuses across all previously deployed applications. The SysAdmin team struggled to diagnose the issue due to a knowledge gap in Kubernetes resource management.

Continued deployment of non-critical applications to Staging, Prod, and UAT environments. Image build failures occurred due to syntax errors, later attributed to non-standardized build paths for application .dll files.
Modifications to the build path introduced a cascading failure, halting subsequent deployments due to invalid Bash variable expansion syntax (utilizing ${} instead of $()).

Deployment of a lower-priority application failed due to an invalid repository name containing an underscore, which violates Kubernetes namespace naming conventions. This also caused Docker build failures; the SysAdmin team misdiagnosed the root cause as an invalid Dockerfile, exacerbating the incident.
Initial deployment of a Python application. Build failures occurred due to missing dependencies in the Dockerfile, highlighting a lack of standardization for new technology stacks.

Deployment failures occurred due to the DevOps team overlooking the inotify instance limit (capped at 512) on the virtual machine. Subsequent pods failed to deploy due to exhausted instances, a setting not disabled by the .NET applications.

Deployment of two applications resulted in one becoming inaccessible. The application bound to the loopback address (127.0.0.1) instead of 0.0.0.0, caused by a non-standardized secrets.json configuration.
Deployment of two applications proceeded with relatively few errors, though minor Bash syntax issues caused the pipeline to fail multiple times before success.

A mandatory update for the Azure Windows agent virtual machine required the SysAdmin team to manually update all previously deployed applications to utilize the new 2022 version to maintain operability.
Successful deployment of two applications with no recorded issues.
Deployment of two applications completed successfully, aside from minor Bash syntax errors and invalid parameter configurations.
Deployment of a backend application utilizing a newer .NET version necessitated manual modifications and adjustments to the Docker image.
The updated .NET version introduced incompatibilities within the production environment, resulting in excessive memory consumption by the deployed pods.

Deployment of a .NET application failed due to an undocumented dependency. The development team was unaware of the issue due to environmental discrepancies (developing on Windows while containers utilized Linux). The SysAdmin team required an overnight effort to resolve the bug.

First deployment utilizing the centralized CI/CD pipeline. The process was delayed due to an unhandled edge case in the central pipeline code and the initial setup of agents across Dev, UAT, and Prod environments.
A pipeline failure in the centralized CI/CD system caused a newly deployed application to fail, resulting from an invalid Bash variable path expansion.
